To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal conditions for DEP-based separation are high conductivity and low values of pH of the suspending fluid, i.e. high zeta potential and low electrokinetic mobiliity.
Electrokinetic force is minimized when suspending medium has high conductivity and low value of pH.

Electrokinetic mobility was measured by μPIV in a straight glass microchannel, and was used to identify the operating parameters that will benefit dielectric trapping and concentration of microorganisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of electrokinetic phenomena in microchannels.
the characterization of electrokinetic phenomena that occur when a DC electric field is applied to a microchannel containing particles.

the characterization of electrokinetic transport of particles suspended in aqueous media inside glass microchannels under the conditions that are employed for insulator-based dielectrophic separation of particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research is focused on the study of the electrokinetics of microparticles in glass microchannels, in order to identify optimal conditions for iDEP-based separation.

this study has been able to identify the operating condition that benefits the dielectrophoresic trapping of biologically relevant particles, i.e., high conductivity and low p H for the suspending fluid.
the electrokinetic transport is a function of the zeta potential, the thickness of the EDL, the conductivity of the suspending media, the viscosity of the fluid and the electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zeta potential is the potential difference between the surface of a charged particle and the bulk fluid.

we were able to determine the conditions that would benefit dielectrophoresic trapping of bi-particles when electrokinesis is present, and these results were proved by carrying dielectrophoretics experiments.
we have developed and demonstrated a new method for the separation of microparticles using iDEP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnitude of the electrokinetics is strongly influenced by the properties of the medium, i.e., conductivity and pH.
the electrokinetic velocity of the particles is strongly influenced by the conductivity of the suspending solution.

the electrokinetic velocity is dependent on the properties of the solution, the magnitude of the electric field, the geometry and surface properties of the microchannel and the size and surface properties of particles.
